prerequisites: It is especially advisable that the student has taken and passed the previous compulsory subjects Machine Mechanics (second year, first semester)
Materials Science and Engineering (second year, first semester)
Elasticity and Strength of Materials (second year, second semester)
Elasticity and Strength of Materials II (third year, first semester)
Advanced Calculation Methods in Mechanical Engineering (fourth year, first semester)

learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Beginnings of research in the field of fracture mechanics.
Fracture mechanics during the post-war period.
Fracture mechanics from 1980 to the present.
Effect of material properties on fracture.
Effect of stress concentration in defects.
The R-curve in elasto-plastic fracture mechanics.
Empirical equations for fatigue crack growth.
Theme 5. Experimental Techniques for Stress and Strain Measurement.
Practical 4: Characterization of fatigue crack growth.
Practical 5: Evaluation of structural integrity using VINDIO software.
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Completion of assignments, cases or proposed exercises

assessment_rules: A minimum score of 4 out of 10 points is required in the written exam to pass the subject. Attendance at laboratory practical sessions is compulsory. Additionally, all practical reports must be submitted on the dates indicated by the professor. Non-attendance at practical sessions or failure to submit reports on time will result in the student not passing the subject.
